title: Pip’s Little Garden
tagline: Check the soil. Find suitable light. Help a seedling grow.
learningGoal: Choose suitable water and light for an already-growing seedling, using a stated soil condition and a demonstrated light comparison.
childTakeaway: A growing plant needs light and water. I check the soil before adding more water.
story: Pip is caring for a small garden. The child helps check what each young plant needs, then revisits the garden over pretend days.
introPip: These little plants are already growing! Let's help them get water and light. Growing takes time, so we'll visit again on pretend days.
conceptImageAlt: Pip, a smiling silver-gray ball with blue seams, sits beside two green seedlings in terracotta pots and a blue watering can in a bright garden.

ageSupport.entry: Read every question aloud, name the pictured choices, and let the child point or tap. Start with the watering-can round and demonstrate the comparison before asking round two.
ageSupport.stretch: Use the optional fifth round to combine light and water. Ask the child to explain or show what is still missing after a one-step plan.

misconception: More water or a taller stem always means a healthier plant; the lesson distinguishes suitable moisture and sturdy growth from excess water and low-light stretching.

rounds.title: A drink for the seedling
rounds.prompt: This seedling's soil is dry. Which thing can give it water?
rounds.sceneAlt: A young plant in dry cracked soil, with a watering can and a hat offered below.
rounds.success: The watering can gives water to the dry soil. We add a little, then check the soil.
hints: Look at the soil. Pip tells us it is dry.
Imagine tipping each thing. Which one can pour water?
A hat does not pour water. The watering can does.
rounds.visualHint: Show a measured small pour into the soil; the soil becomes damp. Keep the plant size unchanged in this moment.
rounds.whyThisRound: Establishes the concrete water-care action before asking the child to diagnose a new plant.

rounds.title: Light makes a difference
rounds.prompt: Both seedlings got water for several pretend days. Which place helped one grow sturdy green leaves?
rounds.sceneAlt: Two watered seedlings after pretend days: one in a dark cupboard and one in a lit garden spot. The stems and leaves differ.
rounds.success: The garden spot gave this seedling suitable light. Its leaves stayed green and its stem grew sturdy.
hints: Look at the leaves and stems, not just how tall the plants are.
Compare the pale thin plant with the sturdy green one. Both got water.
The cupboard plant got too little light. This lit garden spot helped the other grow sturdy leaves.
rounds.visualHint: Replay matched starting seedlings, equal suitable watering, and a day-night sequence. Reveal changes only across pretend days. Outline stems and leaves after the child asks for a hint.
rounds.whyThisRound: Uses an explained comparison to establish light as a need; checks the tempting misconception that the tallest plant must be the healthiest.

rounds.title: Enough water for now
rounds.prompt: We just watered until the soil was damp. Should we check it later, or pour more now?
rounds.sceneAlt: A green seedling with damp soil in a bright spot, above a later-check icon and a pouring-water icon.
rounds.success: It has enough water for now. We check the soil later and water when it needs it.
hints: Remember: the soil is already damp.
Picture more and more water filling the pot. Plants do not need a puddle around their roots.
Choose checking later. Extra water now could make the soil too wet.
rounds.visualHint: On request, compare damp soil with a flooded pot; do not turn the plant instantly brown. Future feedback should show checking moisture, rather than a fixed daily watering rule.
rounds.whyThisRound: Prevents the lesson from becoming 'always add water' and introduces looking before acting.

rounds.title: New plant, same need
rounds.prompt: This different plant already has light, but its soil is dry. What should we do?
rounds.sceneAlt: A different-shaped seedling in a blue container and dry soil, with a dark-cover option and a little-water option.

choices.label: Cover it
choices.spokenLabel: Cover it with a dark lid

choices.label: Give a little water
choices.spokenLabel: Give the soil a little water

rounds.success: The dry soil needs a little water. A different pot and different leaves do not change that need.
hints: What does this plant already have? Pip says it has light.
Look at the dry soil. Would a dark lid bring water?
Give the soil a little water, then check that it is damp.
rounds.visualHint: Keep the changed container and leaf shape throughout feedback. Show a small pour reaching the soil and stop when it is damp; no immediate growth.
rounds.whyThisRound: Tests transfer across plant and container appearance rather than repetition of the first image.

rounds.title: Two needs together — optional stretch
rounds.prompt: This seedling is in a dark cupboard and its soil is dry. Which plan gives it both things it needs?
rounds.sceneAlt: A dry-soil seedling inside a dark cupboard, above three plans combining a lit place, water, or the cupboard.

choices.label: Light only
choices.spokenLabel: Move it into suitable light only

choices.label: Water in cupboard
choices.spokenLabel: Give a little water but keep it in the cupboard

choices.label: Light and water
choices.spokenLabel: Move it into suitable light and give a little water

rounds.success: This plan gives suitable light and water. We keep checking it as pretend days pass.
hints: Pip noticed two things: a dark place and dry soil.
Look for a plan with a lit place and a watering can together.
Light alone leaves the soil dry. Water alone leaves it too dark. Choose suitable light and a little water.
rounds.visualHint: Demonstrate each plan on a duplicate of the same plant. Pause after one need is addressed to name the remaining need; then run the complete plan over pretend days.
rounds.whyThisRound: Optional combination challenge; all action plans are single choices, with no hidden multi-select.

finale: Pip checks the garden over several pretend days. The cared-for seedlings show new leaves. Pip says, 'We gave them what they needed, and we gave them time.'
offlineActivity: With a grown-up, inspect an existing non-toxic potted plant. Gently feel the potting mix and ask whether it needs water; the grown-up follows the plant's own care guidance. Draw or photograph it today and again after a few days.
reviewQuestions: Does the dark-cupboard comparison make the light need clear without teaching that the tallest plant is best?
Is the 'check later' round understandable, or should a future prototype first demonstrate damp versus soaking-wet soil?
Should the two-needs final round be optional for every child, or offered only after the single-need rounds?
designNotes: Review concept only: no game integration, child testing, voice generation, or claims of validated learning outcomes.
The lesson starts with living leafy seedlings. It makes no claim that every seed requires light to germinate.
Water and light are selected learning needs, not a complete plant-care recipe. Species, temperature, nutrients, oxygen, drainage, and watering needs also matter.
The lit garden is a deliberately suitable environment for this illustrative seedling; any window or any amount of sunlight is not automatically suitable.
Dryness is stated in the spoken prompt. Soil color and leaf posture alone are not reliable real-world diagnoses.
Growth and low-light changes happen across pretend days. Small pours change soil moisture, not plant size instantly.
All pictured containers have drainage holes. No universal water amount or watering schedule is prescribed.
Generated art sets the story; the five SVG scenes are the exact question references. The art does not establish species identity or biological timing.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension — Lighting for indoor plants and starting seeds
sources.supports: Suitable light supports growth; insufficient light can produce pale foliage and long thin stems, while excess light can also harm plants.

sources.title: University of Maryland Extension — Care of Vegetable Seedlings
sources.supports: Growing seedlings need sufficient light and suitably moist growing medium; saturated medium can impair roots. Ordinary window light may be insufficient.
